evidence: Receiving DO2 step change at t=46.2h: 7.56 mg/L vs 11.9 mg/L at t=46.0h, then 6.52 mg/L by t=52.0h
Source batches source-1/2/3 all hold DO2 ~10.5-11 mg/L over 46-52h; receiving diverges ~4 mg/L below
Receiving P at 48h = 2.66 g/L, comparable to source ~3.0 g/L — production healthy, arguing against feed reduction
Minimum DO constraint = 2.0 mg/L; current receiving DO ~6.5 mg/L with gentle downward drift, indicating aeration deficit risk
allowed_actions: increase_air = [1.0, 1.15] (no feed cut) vs reduce_feed/combined = [0.8, ...] which reduce substrate and product mass
args.rationale: At 46.2 h the receiving DO2 abruptly fell ~4.5 mg/L below the source-anchored trajectory and continues drifting downward (6.5 mg/L at 52 h), indicating oxygen demand exceeding aeration capacity while production is on track (P=2.66 g/L at 48 h). Increasing air (×1.15) addresses the DO deficit without reducing feed, thus retaining product mass, and carries no oxygen-constraint violation risk (minimum 2.0 mg/L). Alternatives: reduce_feed/combined would trade product mass for DO relief, and stop yields zero counted production; KEEP leaves an ongoing downward DO drift unmanaged.
args.uncertainty: The DO sag could be partly sensor artifact or a transient (the step at 46.2 h is abrupt); if demand is air-transfer-saturated, a 15% air increase may only partially restore DO. No physics tool or post-46h product assay is available to confirm whether the receiving OUR still exceeds the new aeration capacity; continuing online DO2 should be monitored after intervention.
